answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can enforce trust-graph routing, bounding peer influence through capacity paths from verified seeds. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of scarce organic trust edges, as synthetic nodes remain bottlenecked at topological cuts. Even if bots coordinate an intricate sonnet of mutual proofs, an unauthorized transactional voyage cannot cross the cut to pile up like a desert dune. However, this restricts onboarding for new honest agents.
